fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. David says, "In the morning, O LORD, You hear my voice…" (Psalm 5:3). Then he adds, "at daybreak I lay my plea before You and wait in expectation." Morning and daybreak both show up in that one verse.

Evening was a solid guess, friend, and I'd have picked it too after a long day at the ovens. But David names a different time: "In the morning, O LORD, You hear my voice…" (Psalm 5:3). He says "at daybreak" right after that, so this verse is about the sun coming up, not going down.

Right, baker. David says God is not a God who delights in wickedness, and "no evil can dwell with You." (Psalm 5:4). That word "no" doesn't leave any gaps. So the answer is False, since David says none.
Not this time, baker. Being the new guy is rough, believe me. But David says, "the LORD abhors the man of bloodshed and deceit." (Psalm 5:6). Being new has nothing to do with it.

Good guess, friend, but look at the word David uses. He prays, "make straight Your way before me." (Psalm 5:8). That's "Your," so it's the LORD's way, not David's own heart. He asks it right after "Lead me, O LORD, in Your righteousness…"

Yes, baker. David prays, "May You shelter them, that those who love Your name may rejoice in You." (Psalm 5:11). It's a request, and "shelter" is the word he picks for those who take refuge in God. It's a cozy word, like a warm kitchen on a cold night.

Good try, friend, but that's not the word in this verse. David says, "May You shelter them…" (Psalm 5:11). He's asking for shelter for those who take refuge in Him. That fits, because refuge and shelter go together.

Whoa, baker, scatter would be a sad thing to ask for people running to God for safety. David actually says, "May You shelter them…" (Psalm 5:11). He asks the LORD to shelter those who take refuge in Him, which is the opposite of scattering them.
